# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# fields: COMMAND_RPC_REFRESH::response_t, src/wallet/wallet_rpc_server_commands_defs.h:2066-2075
#         -> { blocks_fetched u64, received_money bool }. NO status/untrusted.
# request: { start_height u64 } (:2056-2063), KV_SERIALIZE_OPT default 0 (:2061).
# §5c's `wallet refresh` payload is exactly these two keys.
# THIS CALL RUNS UNDER THE 120 s refresh DEADLINE (§2d, timeouts.refresh_sec), the longest of the six
#         settings-backed ones apart from open_wallet's 300 s -- and it is the call most likely to be
#         killed at it on a wallet with a restore height. A wallet call killed at its deadline while
#         status.wallet.blocks_behind > WALLET_BEHIND_BLOCKS (100) is classified `wallet_syncing`,
#         NOT a stall, and does NOT arm the §2d breaker: a breaker that fires on correct behaviour is
#         the breaker an agent disables. Pair --delay-ms with --scenario behind (get_height-behind.json)
#         to exercise that branch against the mock.
# received_money: false HERE because blocks_fetched is small and nothing arrived. A test that wants
#         the true branch uses --scenario; there is no such fixture yet because nothing in §4.1, §5
#         or §7a branches on it -- §5c renders it and stops.
# NOT IN DESIGN.md §8's deliverable list; added by Phase 0 with its reason recorded in
# decisions/phase0-mock.md and tests/fixtures/README.md ("Additions"). The reason: `wallet refresh`
# is an AMBER row in §4b, §5c fixes its payload, and the bar widget's action table (§6.3) binds
# "Refresh wallet" to it -- so the plugin smoke path needs an answer too.
